propositions: Pandoc per-field invocation incurs ~0.3s spawn overhead per field, causing serial reconciles to stall ~20 min; batching contiguous safe units into one invocation reduces subprocess cost.

Pathological inputs cause pandoc jira-reader to hang indefinitely (13.5 min observed); pypandoc's convert_text API has no timeout, so a hard timeout via proc.communicate() and process-group reaping is required.
Direct subprocess.run(timeout=) kills only the direct child; CPU-spinning grandchildren survive; process-group reaping via rebar._proc.reap_process_group must kill the entire session.
Dangerous units (those that corrupt pandoc) must bypass pandoc entirely and be spliced verbatim at their original positions; safe units are batched and rendered together.
On timeout or non-zero exit of a safe-run batch, that entire segment degrades to verbatim Markdown without raising an exception; dangerous units and other segments remain unaffected.
The pypandoc-binary wheel and bundled pandoc binary must be pinned by version in pyproject.toml, the pin verified in CI, and GPL license recorded in SBOM/notice.
